program: SNAP — formerly "Food Supplement Program" in Maine's own rule titles; DHHS's current rule and consumer materials now use "SNAP," see PROVENANCE.md
agency: Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), Office for Family Independence (OFI)
admin_note: Maine is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — OFI runs SNAP centrally, through 16 regional/district field offices that carry out state policy with no independent county-level policy authority (structurally similar to this roster's Nebraska, Connecticut, Ohio, and most other state-administered packs, and distinct from county-option-in states like CA/NY/MN/WI/VA). GENUINE NAMING-TRANSITION FINDING this pack found and verified directly from primary sources: Maine's own current SNAP rules manual (10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 301) is titled, in its own header, "SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM (SNAP) RULES (formerly FOOD SUPPLEMENT PROGRAM)" — this pack reads this as dispositive: "SNAP" is Maine's current, correct name, and "Food Supplement Program" is the RETIRED former name, still visible in some URL slugs (maine.gov/dhhs/ofi/programs-services/food-supplement) and older materials but no longer the department's own preferred label. FLAGSHIP CORRECTION this pack found: a secondary source (prisonpolicy.org, a generally careful outlet, in a February 2026 50-state survey) categorized Maine as having NOT opted out of the federal SNAP drug-felony ban. This pack fetched Maine's own statute directly (22 M.R.S. § 3104(14)) and found the opposite is true and has been law for years: Maine HAS fully opted out — a person otherwise eligible for SNAP "may not be denied assistance because the person has been convicted of a drug-related felony." This pack flags this correction explicitly rather than silently repeating the secondary source (see criminal-justice-disqualifications supplement) — Maine DOES retain a separate, much narrower disqualification for certain post-1/1/2018 violent-crime and sexual-assault felony convictions under 22 M.R.S. § 3104(15), which this pack reads as the likely source of the secondary source's confusion. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING: Maine's own current SNAP Rules Appendix (Section 999-3, Chart 3) carries a 165% FPL income column, but — unlike a BBCE ceiling — this pack read the chart's own header precisely and found it is scoped narrowly to a "separate household" determination for elderly/disabled individuals living with others (Section 111-1(2)(c)), NOT Maine's actual BBCE gross-income ceiling, which is a full 200% FPL (Chart 4) — a materially different, much higher figure a reader skimming only "165%" could easily conflate with the state's real categorical-eligibility ceiling (see income-pathways supplement). THIRD FLAGSHIP, TIME-SENSITIVE FINDING: OBBBA (H.R. 1, July 2025) restricted the nationwide "Heat & Eat" mechanism that let many states auto-qualify a household for the full Standard Utility Allowance via a small LIHEAP payment; Maine's own DHHS blog post states this now limits automatic SUA-via-LIHEAP eligibility to households with an elderly or disabled member, affecting an estimated 980 Maine households, effective Fall 2025 — households not otherwise elderly/disabled and without a directly-billed heating/cooling cost may see their utility deduction drop (see shelter-utility-deductions supplement). Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DHHS office, the same caution this roster already carries for CA/NY/MN/WI/OH/NC/NJ/VA/GA/IN/TN/MO/MD/CO/SC/AL/LA/KY/OK/CT/UT/IA/AR/MS/KS/NM/NE.
system: OFI processes SNAP centrally; applicants apply online through My Maine Connection (www1.maine.gov/benefits/account/login.html, DHHS's self-service portal), by phone through the SNAP hotline (1-855-797-4357 / 1-800-442-6003), by mail to the Office for Family Independence (114 Corn Shop Lane, Farmington, ME 04938), or in person at a regional DHHS office. Most households are certified under simplified/periodic reporting; this pack did not find a directly-fetched, dated 10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 301 certification-period section confirming exact standard certification-period lengths by household category with the same confidence as this pack's dollar-figure findings — flagged as a disclosed gap, see freshness.json.

verification.gates: maine.gov, legislature.maine.gov, and fna.usda.gov all returned clean HTTP 200 to direct fetches with no bot-detection wall. The only complications this pack found were (1) two attempted WebFetch calls to fna.usda.gov policy-memo pages (waiver-termination, waiver-reinstatement) that timed out — resolved by reading the ABAWD Waivers FY2025-2029 index page directly instead, which contained the needed Maine-specific waiver-response date without requiring those two memo pages, and (2) Maine's own SNAP Rule #244 Rule Pages PDF being a tracked-changes/redline document whose FFY-history rows partially overlap in pdftotext extraction for Charts 1-4 (old and new figures visually merged) — resolved by cross-checking every FFY2026 figure this pack cites against either a clean, non-overlapping row in the same table or Maine's live consumer page, and disclosing the one figure (Standard Deduction, household size 4) that could not be fully reconciled this way.
